📚 Today you learned

Reconciliation Risk — When Your Records Don't Match Your Broker

In forex you mostly watch your own MT4/5 blotter — it's the account of record in real time. In equities, you've got at least two ledgers that can disagree: the broker's fill log (the source of truth) and whatever tracking sheet, app, or portfolio file you keep alongside it. Today's GOOG situation is the exact failure mode: your stop at $333.90 was likely crossed multiple sessions running, the plain STOP should have fired as a market order on trigger, but there's no fill logged anywhere this system can see, and the price feed used to check has been down again today. That's not a P&L problem yet — it's a state problem. You don't actually know if you're long GOOG right now. The fix is always the same: broker platform is the only authority, reconcile to it directly rather than trusting a secondary record, and do it immediately when a stop should plausibly have fired. A tracking sheet that's a day stale is a convenience; a tracking sheet that's a day stale when a stop should have triggered is a liability.

Also today: Order Fill Confirmation — the broker message/trade confirm that proves an order executed; never assume a stop filled just because price traded through the trigger, especially in thin or gapping conditions.
